books.section: Topic 3.12 Movement in the Early Republic

stimulus.text: Paraphrase: After the Revolution, the United States tried to settle Native land claims north of the Ohio River by treaty. In 1784, the Treaty of Fort Stanwix was made with the Iroquois Confederacy, which ceded land north of the Ohio. But the Iroquois did not live on most of that land, and the Shawnee, Delaware, and Miami who did live there were not part of the talks and protested the cession. In 1785, the Treaty of Fort McIntosh was made with the Wyandotte, Delaware, Chippewa, and Ottawa, who ceded lands in the region. In 1789, the Treaty of Fort Harmar dealt with more lands north of the Ohio. None of these treaties settled control of the region, and the powerful Shawnee stayed outside them.
stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase drawn from Barron’s Premium 2027, Chapter 5, Topic 3.12.

source: original; stimulus paraphrased from Barron’s Premium 2027, Chapter 5, Topic 3.12.
stem: Why did these treaties fail to settle control of the Ohio country?

options.text: Because Congress never signed them and they had no legal force at all.
options.misconception: The treaties were signed and in force; the trouble was that the Shawnee stayed outside them.

options.text: Because the powerful Shawnee stayed outside all three treaties.
Because the treaties gave all the land back to Britain instead.
options.misconception: Background: Britain kept its forts in the region, but no treaty gave the land to Britain.

options.text: Because the treaties banned all American settlement north of the Ohio River.
options.misconception: The treaties ceded land for settlement; they did not ban it.

rationales.A: The treaties were signed and in force; the trouble was the signers, not the signatures.
rationales.B: The Shawnee stayed outside all three treaties, and the peoples who lived on the ceded land were not at the talks, so no treaty settled control on the ground.
rationales.C: No treaty returned land to Britain; Britain simply kept its forts.
rationales.D: The treaties gave land for settlement; they placed no ban on it.
rationales.general:
1. Fort Stanwix was signed with the Iroquois, who did not live on most of the land ceded.
2. The Shawnee, Delaware, and Miami who lived there were not part of the talks.
3. Those nations protested that their land was given away without their consent.
4. So the treaties failed because the Shawnee stayed outside them, leaving control unsettled.
Remember: a treaty settles land only if the people who live there agree to it.
